idiom_name: ASP.NET Core MVC controller action returning View(model) with Razor
implementation_notes: The framework is the controller and dispatcher: MVC endpoint routing picks the controller, instantiates it per request, and an action returning View(model) produces a ViewResult that the Razor engine resolves to Views/<Controller>/<Action>.cshtml and renders with the typed model. What replaces the classic structure is the framework's action invoker plus ViewResult, so the worker is an action method over injected services, and TagHelpers/Razor helpers occupy the view-helper slot; the hand-written front controller (one endpoint plus command objects) is justified only for a genuinely custom dispatch pipeline, for example a plug-in host that must route to actions discovered at runtime.
pitfalls: ViewData/ViewBag is a dynamic dictionary: a mistyped key yields an empty region instead of a compile error, so pass a strongly typed model or view model type.
Blocking on async service calls (.Result/.Wait()) inside an action starves the thread pool; make actions async Task<IActionResult> end to end.
Authorization belongs in filters/policies around the controller - putting the check inside each action duplicates it and the next action will forget it.
